title: Definition
body_md:
For $\epsilon\ge0$, define
\[
\mathcal B_\epsilon(P)=\{a\in\mathcal A:\Delta_P(a)\le\epsilon\}.
\]
We call the nested family $\mathscr B(P)=\{\mathcal B_\epsilon(P):\epsilon\ge0\}$ the \emph{Bayes-regret filtration}, or simply the \emph{regret filtration}.
head: environment
name: Regret-acceptable action set

label: prop:regret-reconstruction
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:regret-reconstruction}
For every $a\in\mathcal A$,
\[
\Delta_P(a)
=
\inf\{\epsilon\ge0:a\in\mathcal B_\epsilon(P)\}.
\]
Hence $\mathscr B(P)$ and the centered risk $a\mapsto R_P(a)-R_P^*$ determine one another.
head: environment
name: Reconstruction of Bayes regret

title: Proof
body_md: By definition, $a\in\mathcal B_\epsilon(P)$ if and only if $\Delta_P(a)\le\epsilon$.  The admissible tolerances are therefore $[\Delta_P(a),\infty)$.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
An approximate posterior $Q$ is \emph{$\epsilon$-adequate} for target posterior $P$ if
\[
\mathcal B_0(Q)\cap\mathcal B_\epsilon(P)\neq\varnothing.
\]
If the Bayes action under $Q$ is unique, this reduces to $\Delta_P(\Gamma(Q))\le\epsilon$.  In that case we call $Q$ \emph{strictly $\epsilon$-adequate} when $\Delta_P(\Gamma(Q))<\epsilon$.
head: environment
name: Decision adequacy

label: prop:repair-contraction-v2
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:repair-contraction-v2}
For every $\epsilon\ge0$,
\[
\mathcal R_{P,Q_0}(\epsilon)
=
\inf_{a\in\mathcal B_\epsilon(P)}I_{Q_0}(a).
\]
head: environment
name: Repair as contraction onto the acceptable set

title: Proof
body_md: Since $\mathcal G_\epsilon(P)=\bigcup_{a\in\mathcal B_\epsilon(P)}\mathcal C_a$, partial minimization over the union gives the result.
head: environment

label: thm:local-repair-robustness-v2
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:local-repair-robustness-v2}
Under (M1)--(M4) of Appendix~\ref{app:regularity-moving-target}, for each fixed $c\ge0$,
\[
\frac{\mathcal R_{P_t,Q_0}(t^2c)}{t^2}
\longrightarrow
r(c;\delta)
:=
\min_h
\left\{
\frac12h^\top J_Ih:
\frac12(h-\delta)^\top G(h-\delta)\le c
\right\}.
\]
For each fixed $c>c_0$, so that the baseline is locally strictly adequate,
\[
\frac{\mathcal M_{P_t,Q_0}(t^2c)}{t^2}
\longrightarrow
m(c;\delta)
:=
\min_h
\left\{
\frac12h^\top J_Ih:
\frac12(h-\delta)^\top G(h-\delta)\ge c
\right\}.
\]
When the limiting minimizer is unique, information-minimizing repaired actions converge after rescaling to the repair minimizer, and every asymptotically minimizing sequence of strict-failure actions converges after rescaling to the failure minimizer.
head: environment
name: Local repair and robustness

label: thm:effective-dimension
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:effective-dimension}
With the convention $\gamma_{d+1}=0$, for every $r\in\{0,\ldots,d\}$,
\[
\mathcal E_r^*(\rho)=\rho\gamma_{r+1}.
\]
An optimal retained subspace is $S_r^*=\operatorname{span}\{v_1,\ldots,v_r\}$, with $S_d^*=E$.  The smallest rank that guarantees omitted regret at most $\epsilon$ is
\[
 d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\epsilon;\rho)
 =
 \min\{r:\rho\gamma_{r+1}\le\epsilon\}
 =
 \#\{i:\rho\gamma_i>\epsilon\}.
\]
head: environment
name: Optimal information-bounded decision representation

title: Proof
body_md:
Whiten action space by the information metric.  Let $x=J_I^{1/2}h$ and $L=J_I^{1/2}S$.  Then $\mathcal H_\rho$ maps to $\{x:\|x\|^2\le2\rho\}$ and
\[
\inf_{s\in S}\frac12(h-s)^\top G(h-s)
=
\inf_{y\in L}\frac12(x-y)^\top A(x-y).
\]
Because $A\succ0$, the map $z=A^{1/2}x$ is invertible.  The information ball is mapped to the ellipsoid
\[
\mathcal K_\rho
=
\left\{A^{1/2}x:\|x\|^2\le2\rho\right\},
\]
whose Euclidean principal semiaxes are $\sqrt{2\rho\gamma_1},\ldots,\sqrt{2\rho\gamma_d}$.  As $L$ ranges over $r$-dimensional subspaces, $A^{1/2}L$ ranges over all $r$-dimensional Euclidean subspaces.  For $r<d$, the Kolmogorov $r$-width of this ellipsoid is its $(r+1)$st semiaxis.  Squaring and multiplying by $1/2$ gives $\mathcal E_r^*(\rho)=\rho\gamma_{r+1}$, and the optimal subspace maps back to $\operatorname{span}\{v_1,\ldots,v_r\}$.  The case $r=d$ gives zero residual error.  The formula for $d_{\mathrm{eff}}$ follows.
head: environment

label: prop:ensemble-dimension
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:ensemble-dimension}
For every $r\in\{0,\ldots,d\}$,
\[
\overline{\mathcal E}_r^*
=
\frac12\sum_{i>r}\zeta_i.
\]
Consequently, an average-case effective dimension at tolerance $\epsilon$ is
\[
 d_{\mathrm{ens}}(\epsilon)
=
\min\left\{
 r:
 \frac12\sum_{i>r}\zeta_i\le\epsilon
\right\}.
\]
head: environment
name: Target-ensemble representation

title: Proof
body_md: Let $Y=G^{1/2}\Delta$ and $L=G^{1/2}S$.  Then $\overline{\mathcal E}(S)=\tfrac12\mathbb E[\operatorname{dist}^2(Y,L)]$.  The rank-$r$ minimizer is the principal-component, or proper-orthogonal-decomposition, subspace of the second-moment matrix $K=\mathbb E[YY^\top]$, and the minimum residual mean-square error is the sum of the omitted eigenvalues \cite{jolliffe2002pca}.
head: environment

label: prop:restricted-repair-contraction
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:restricted-repair-contraction}
For every $\epsilon\ge0$,
\[
\mathcal R_{P,Q_0,\mathcal Q}(\epsilon)
=
\inf_{a\in\mathcal B_\epsilon(P)}I_{Q_0,\mathcal Q}(a)
=
\inf_{a\in\operatorname{Act}(\mathcal Q)\cap\mathcal B_\epsilon(P)}
I_{Q_0,\mathcal Q}(a).
\]
Consequently
\[
\mathcal R_{P,Q_0,\mathcal Q}(\epsilon)\ge\mathcal R_{P,Q_0}(\epsilon).
\]
head: environment
name: Restricted repair contraction

title: Proof
body_md: Apply the same partial-minimization argument as in Proposition~\ref{prop:repair-contraction-v2} to the union of restricted action fibers.  The inequality follows because the restricted problem minimizes over $\mathcal Q\subseteq\mathfrak C_{Q_0}$, a subset of the ambient candidate class.
head: environment

label: prop:restricted-local-information-v2
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Restricted tangent Fisher energy

label: prop:restricted-family-coverage-v2
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:restricted-family-coverage-v2}
For every $\rho>0$,
\[
\mathcal E_\rho(T)=\rho\eta_T.
\]
Consequently the tangent image gives a uniform local regret guarantee $\epsilon$ over all ambient target displacements of information cost at most $\rho$ if and only if
\[
\rho\eta_T\le\epsilon.
\]
head: environment
name: Restricted-family coverage certificate

title: Proof
body_md: Whiten with $z=J_I^{1/2}h$.  The information constraint becomes $\left\lVert z\right\rVert^2\le2\rho$, and the objective becomes $\tfrac12z^\top J_I^{-1/2}R_TJ_I^{-1/2}z$.  The maximum over the Euclidean ball is $\rho$ times the largest eigenvalue.
head: environment

label: prop:app-v2-exact-projection
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Exact local I-projection

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $Q\in\mathcal C_a$.  Infinite-KL competitors cannot improve on the finite value attained by $Q_a^*$.  If $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q\|Q_0)<\infty$, assumption (I1) gives $\mathbb E_Q\psi_a=0$.  The entropy variational inequality gives, for every admissible multiplier $\lambda$,
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q\|Q_0)
\ge
\lambda^\top\mathbb E_Q\psi_a-\Lambda(a,\lambda)
=
-\Lambda(a,\lambda).
\]
Taking $\lambda=\lambda(a)$ gives the lower bound $-\Lambda(a,\lambda(a))$, and the tilted law in \eqref{eq:app-v2-exponential-tilt} attains it.
head: environment

label: lem:app-v2-compact-minima
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:app-v2-compact-minima}
Let $F_t,F\subset\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty compact sets contained in a common compact set $K$, and suppose
\[
F_t\xrightarrow{d_H}F.
\]
Let $\phi_t,\phi:K\to\mathbb R$ be continuous and satisfy
\[
\sup_{h\in K}|\phi_t(h)-\phi(h)|\to0.
\]
Then
\[
\inf_{h\in F_t}\phi_t(h)
\longrightarrow
\inf_{h\in F}\phi(h).
\]
If the limiting minimizer is unique, every sequence of exact minimizers converges to it.
head: environment
name: Stability of constrained minima

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $h_t$ minimize $\phi_t$ on $F_t$.  Compactness gives convergent subsequences.  If $h_{t_n}\to h$, Hausdorff convergence implies $h\in F$, and uniform convergence of $\phi_t$ together with continuity of $\phi$ gives
\[
\phi_{t_n}(h_{t_n})\to\phi(h)\ge\inf_F\phi.
\]
Conversely, for any $h\in F$, Hausdorff convergence gives $\widetilde h_t\in F_t$ with $\widetilde h_t\to h$, so
\[
\limsup_t\inf_{F_t}\phi_t
\le
\lim_t\phi_t(\widetilde h_t)
=
\phi(h).
\]
Taking the infimum over $h\in F$ proves convergence of the values.  Uniqueness of the limiting minimizer then forces convergence of the full minimizer sequence.
head: environment

label: prop:app-v2-kappa-equality
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:app-v2-kappa-equality}
The restricted and ambient tangent costs agree for every $h\in S_T$ if and only if
\[
B^*J_I(S_T)\subseteq T.
\]
With the convention $\kappa_T=1$ when $S_T=\{0\}$, this is equivalent to $\kappa_T=1$ exactly when the restricted tangent contains the ambient minimum-information lift of every decision displacement it can realize.
head: environment
name: Equality condition for local information efficiency

title: Proof
body_md:
For each reachable $h$, the ambient minimum-norm solution $s_h^*=B^*J_Ih$ is unique because it is the orthogonal projection of the origin onto the affine space
\[
\{s\in\mathcal H:B[s]=h\}.
\]
If $s_h^*\in T$, it is feasible for the restricted problem and the two minima agree.  Conversely, if the minima agree, a restricted minimizer must attain the unique ambient minimum norm, hence must equal $s_h^*$ and therefore lie in $T$.
head: environment
